purpose: Find an observable guest display for the authorized NTSD Windows reference installation while the host screen is locked.
scope: Read-only official UTM4.7.5 source/docs, installed bundle inventory, two defaults keys, task VM filenames/config and process identity. No API library loaded or SPICE/QMP connection created.

officialSources.finding: SDK advertises Unix socket connections and display screenshots. This is library capability, not an installed screenshot CLI.
Documents automatic screenshots and a separate disk-save preference; screenshot normally lives in the VM package.
60-second timer calls takeScreenshot; saveScreenshot is separate and writes screenshot.png when enabled. The docs say30s, so this versioned source is more precise for the installed version.
SPICE takeScreenshot updates the in-memory property and does not call saveScreenshot.
Default suspend-state save and terminal stop call saveScreenshot. determineSnapshotSupport rejects GL display hardware and NVMe. Both conditions occur in the unchanged VM config.
suspend saving true is a documented state-changing operation; it is not a read-only screenshot request.

conclusions: Waiting for the periodic timer alone does not establish a fresh disk PNG.
Static source/config inference: saved-state capture is unsupported for this VM; not experimentally attempted.
No existing disk screenshot or installed direct screenshot command established. A second SPICE client could affect the current session; its coexistence was not established or tested.
